part.name: Computer mouse housing with scroll wheel

part_functions.name: handheld pointing-device enclosure
part_functions.function: Provides an ergonomic mouse-shaped body that supports the user's hand and encloses the intended internal electronics.

part_functions.name: scroll input interface
part_functions.function: Provides a centrally positioned rounded wheel intended to rotate about the transverse X axis for scrolling or related user input.

section_functions.name: hand support and enclosure
section_functions.function: The broad top deck, curved flanks, nose, heel, and underside form a continuous load-bearing enclosure with a rounded palm-supporting profile.

section_functions.name: structural relationship
section_functions.function: The outer body surrounds and supports the central wheel well; the left and right flanks are approximately bilaterally symmetric about the longitudinal center plane.

feature_functions.name: ergonomic surface
feature_functions.function: Its smoothly varying B-spline surfaces distribute hand contact and transition continuously between the top, sides, front nose, rear heel, and bottom.

feature_functions.name: body support
feature_functions.function: The top deck supports hand loads, the side flanks provide lateral grip surfaces, and the underside provides the device's supporting base.

feature_functions.name: adjacency
feature_functions.function: The listed surfaces form an adjacent walk from the top through the left flank, front nose, right flank, underside, and rear heel.

brep_faces.semantic_role: Broad convex top and palm-support deck, including the boundary around the central wheel-well opening.

Rounded right-side flank approximately symmetric to the left flank.
Broad underside and supporting base surface near minimum Y.
Curved rear heel closure at the negative-Z end of the mouse.

section_functions.name: wheel clearance and location
section_functions.function: The narrow, upward-open rectangular well provides clearance around the scroll wheel while locating it near the longitudinal centerline.

section_functions.name: functional relationship
section_functions.function: The well is integrated into the outer body and laterally retains the separate wheel while permitting its rounded perimeter to remain exposed above the deck.

feature_functions.name: lateral guidance
feature_functions.function: Opposed planar sidewalls constrain transverse movement of the wheel and establish its X-axis alignment.

feature_functions.name: clearance pocket
feature_functions.function: The end walls and recessed floor provide operating clearance around the wheel; no discrete axle bore or fastener feature is modeled.

feature_functions.name: structural relationship
feature_functions.function: The recess is centered in the body and surrounds the wheel with approximately parallel sidewalls and end walls.

section_functions.name: rotary user input
section_functions.function: The separate rounded wheel presents a finger-contacting perimeter and is intended to rotate about an axis approximately parallel to X.

section_functions.name: structural relationship
section_functions.function: The wheel is centered within the body recess, with its two planar end faces normal to the transverse rotation axis and its toroidal surfaces forming the exposed rim.

features.name: Toroidal scroll-wheel rim and end faces

feature_functions.name: finger contact
feature_functions.function: The two adjoining toroidal faces create a smooth, crowned perimeter for comfortable traction under a fingertip.

feature_functions.name: axial definition
feature_functions.function: The opposed planar circular end faces define the wheel width and indicate a common transverse X-oriented rotation axis.

feature_functions.name: retention relationship
feature_functions.function: The wheel occupies the open recess as a disconnected solid and is laterally bounded by the well sidewalls, although an axle or bearing interface is not explicitly represented.
